_doc: Picture/sound contract for plane-door-midflight. 30 fps. Frames come from voice/frames.txt (word start frames). Visual reactions land 0-3 frames before their word.

places.cabin: inside an airliner by day (this video's own place): the exit door with its big red handle in the cross-aisle, the narrow lavatory door beside it, rows of blue seats with windows, overhead bins
places.sky: open sky above a sea of clouds (this video's own place): the airliner as a flat cartoon side view, a cutaway of it, a pressure gauge, the plug diagram; with a runway for the landing
places.garden: Gus's back garden (kit town place, plain lawn): four cars stacked on a door, the suction cup on his helmet

shots.what: HOOK, already moving. Full shot at the exit door: Gus in pyjamas and fishbowl helmet hangs on the big red handle with both hands, leaning far back, one foot braced on the door, and yanks three times (f5, f23, f39); sweat drops fly, the door does not move a hair. Lens low and a little rolled, pushing in.

Cut outside on 'seven miles up': the airliner from the side, cruising level over a sea of clouds, small in a huge blue sky; the lens pulls back and back so it gets smaller. Clouds drift past. A calm glint on the fuselage on 'no danger' (f106). Whoosh at f124, white flash at f139.

Looking down the cabin at the first seat row: the neighbor at the window, the wife in the middle, Gus in the aisle seat asleep with a sleep bubble, afternoon sun in the windows. On 'woke' the bubble pops (f198), he jolts awake, eyes wide, then stretches both arms up with a yawn (f212); glide in on him centred on f200.

At the exit door, medium full shot: sleepy Gus shuffles up to it, a thought bubble with a toilet in it pops over his head on 'thinks' (f242), and his hand lands on the red handle (f266). Slow push-in.

Back on the seat row, two-shot: the wife screams, hands up, mouth wide (f289); the lens glides to the neighbor at the window, who grabs his seat belt and pulls it tight across his belly (f331, click f354), eyes huge. The aisle seat is empty.

The exit door, full shot: Gus pulls harder, both hands on the handle, leaning back until he is a diagonal line (grunt f380). On 'Nothing' the door answers with one tiny glint (f399): it has not moved.

Same door, closer and rolled: he plants a foot on the door (bonk f431), shoe squeaking (f445), heaves with all his weight (f452); on 'Still nothing' his hands slip (f461) and he sits down hard on the carpet (thud f473). The door is exactly where it was.

Dead stop. Gus on his feet again in front of the shut door, puzzled; on 'isn't that weak' he flexes an arm, fist by his helmet, with a proud glint on it (f523); on 'what's holding' a big question mark pops over the door (f544) and the lens pushes past him toward the handle.

Outside: the airliner cruising, closer than before, a few lonely air dots drifting past it, far apart (they thin out on 'thin', f638). A round pressure gauge pops in above the plane (f662), needle on full with a little house at that mark; on 'a fifth' the needle sinks to the lowest fifth (f676 to f692), where a tiny plane marks the dial; the house mark blinks on 'ground' (f726).

The same airliner as a cutaway, from the cut (f745): inside, the cabin is packed with air dots, outside there are few. On 'pumped up like a tire' the fuselage swells in two pump strokes (f764, f783). On 'all that air wants out' fat blue arrows pop out of the cabin against the skin, pushing outward (f809, f828).

Inside, the exit door seen at an angle, filling the frame. A row of blue arrows leans on it from the cabin side, pressing (f853). On 'every square inch' one small yellow square lights up on the door with a sparkle (f875). Slow push toward the square.

Same framing, continuous: an iron weight marked 8 lands on the yellow square (thud f923) and hangs there, pressing. On 'outside pushes back' a tiny pale arrow taps feebly at the door's window from the other side (f992) and gives up.

Same door, continuous: yellow squares spread from the first one over the whole door, row after row, top to bottom, until it is covered by a grid (f1016 to f1054). The lens eases back to hold the whole door.

Same door: on 'Add them up' a swarm of little weights rushes together in front of the grid (f1080 to f1104) and on 'twenty thousand' one giant iron weight marked 20,000 slams against the door (f1125), shaking the frame. The door holds.

Gus's garden, wide and tall: a plane door lies on the lawn and four cartoon cars drop onto it one after the other into a stack (f1170, f1181, f1192, f1203), the top one honks (f1214). Gus stands beside the tower in his pyjamas looking up, then down at the door under it.
Garden two-shot: his wife sticks a red suction cup onto the glass of Gus's fishbowl helmet (pop f1258) and tugs at it twice (f1277, f1290); the cup holds and Gus sways along with every tug.

Close on the cup on the helmet glass: 'no glue', she lets go and it stays, a question mark over it (f1312). On 'air pushing on one side' three blue arrows pop in pressing on the cup from outside (f1353). She pulls once more and it comes off with a pop on 'side' (f1381); Gus blinks.
The exit door head on, shut, its outline shimmering (f1401). On 'plug' a bathtub plug on a chain pops up beside it with a sparkle (f1425): same idea. Slow push-in.

Diagram against the sky, seen from above: the cabin wall cut through, with the door as a wedge sitting in its hole, wide side toward the cabin, cabin air (dense dots, blue arrows) pressing it into the frame. On 'bigger than its hole' it tries to go out and bumps twice (f1462, f1474). On 'come in' it slides inward (f1506), on 'swings out' it turns edge-on and leaves through the hole (f1529 to f1544).

Garden: a rope from the door under the four-car stack over Gus's shoulder. He leans into it almost flat (grunt f1561), slippers scrabbling on the grass and throwing dust (f1590 to f1630), groans (f1612). The stack does not move.
Cabin, at the shut exit door: Gus lets go of the handle and slumps, arms hanging, beaten; the door gleams, untouched (twinkle f1656). Medium shot, gentle push-in.
Same spot, closer: on 'Unluckily' his eyes go wide (gulp f1691); knees together, he hops from foot to foot (f1717 to f1760), a toilet thought bubble popping back over his head on 'bathroom' (f1735).
The airliner parked on a runway under a low calm sky, wheels down. On 'lets go' its front door pops open by itself and swings wide, easy as a cupboard (f1787, creak to f1805); a bird chirps (f1812).

PAYOFF. Gus shuffles left along the wall to the narrow lavatory door (steps f1830 to f1856), its little latch window glowing green; on 'the one door' it sparkles (f1877) and he reaches for the knob, hopeful (click f1916). On 'It's taken' the latch window snaps to red with a buzz (f1936) and his face falls; hold on him, knees together, to the last word.
